newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola sees roughly $4.0 bln in '96 operating profit.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola sees roughly $4.0 bln in '96 operating profit.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co K.O Chairman Roberto Goizueta said the soft drink giant expects an operating profit this year of roughly $4.0 billion. He said 80 percent of that will be generated outside the United States.
"Out of our give-or-take $4 billion of operating income that we will have this year, 80 percent will be outside of the United States," Goizueta told the Executives Club here.
Coca-Cola had operating profit of 1995 of $4.18 billion, which excluded non-recurring items.

Oppenheimer analyst Roy Burry said Coca-Cola's operating profit in 1996 is expected to be lower due, in part, to inventory reductions and reserves for future costs. Burry said he projects Coca-Cola's operating income at about $4.09 billion in 1996.
Goizueta also said Coca-Cola now has equity positions in bottlers that account for about 44 percent of its worldwide volume. That volume will be about 14 billion cases of product this year, he added.
Commenting on the growth of Coca-Cola's international business, Goizueta said the company will have 23 bottling plants in China by the end of the first quarter, up from 18 plants now.

"Coca-Cola used to be a large American company with a sizeable international business," Goizueta said. "Now we are a large international company with a large American business and we happen to be headquartered in Atlanta."
